title: Algorithm Visualizer
summary: To visualize loop execution (for/while), conditional branching (if/else), and array iterations.
spec_text: A step-through visualizer where a standard loop generates a 2D grid of shapes. The student can step forward or backward through the loop iterations. A conditional logic threshold determines the color or shape drawn, which the student can adjust via sliders to immediately see how conditional changes affect the overall pattern.

title: Robot Arm Kinematics
summary: To teach translation, rotation, scaling, and the matrix stack (`push()` and `pop()`).
spec_text: A hierarchical, multi-segment robotic arm drawn using transformations. The student can independently rotate and translate each joint. A toggle visualizes the local coordinate axes for each segment, demonstrating how `translate()` and `rotate()` compound, and how `push()`/`pop()` isolate these transformations.

title: Harmonic Oscillator
summary: To map trigonometric functions (sine/cosine) and polar coordinates to animation and motion.
spec_text: A real-time graphing tool mapping a rotating circle (polar coordinates) to a standard sine/cosine wave (Cartesian). The student can adjust the amplitude and frequency of the oscillator and observe the resulting Lissajous curves or wave patterns.

title: Terrain Generator
summary: To contrast pure randomness with smooth Perlin noise and understand noise detail.
spec_text: Generates a 1D and 2D landscape visualization. The student can toggle between standard `random()` and `noise()` to see the structural difference. Sliders allow the adjustment of noise scale, octaves, and falloff, directly altering the generated terrain profile.

title: Particle Physics Engine
summary: To teach vector addition, velocity, acceleration, mass, and environmental forces.
spec_text: A sandbox containing an emitter that shoots particles. The student can manipulate environmental vector forces like gravity and wind. The simulation calculates the sum of forces (F=ma) applied to the particles' velocity vectors, demonstrating realistic physics trajectories.

title: Interactive Sandbox
summary: To handle asynchronous user events (mouse, keyboard, touch) and device inputs.
spec_text: A unified canvas that acts as an event logger and interactive toy. It visually responds to clicks, double-clicks, dragging, and keypresses. An overlay displays the exact p5.js event variables (`mouseX`, `keyIsPressed`, `keyCode`) triggering in real-time.

title: UI Component Playground
summary: To teach the integration of HTML DOM elements (sliders, buttons, inputs) over the p5.js canvas.
spec_text: Demonstrates absolute and relative positioning of DOM elements over a canvas. The student creates generic DOM elements and uses sliders to adjust their `position()` and `style()`, visually breaking them out of the standard canvas flow to build a UI overlay.

title: Data Flow Debugger
summary: To visualize standard JS mechanics like array mapping, filtering, object destructuring, and scope.
spec_text: A visual data-pipeline tool. An input array of objects is passed through a sequence of higher-order functions (`map`, `filter`, `reduce`). The student configures the filter conditions or map transformations and sees the visual output representation (e.g., shapes changing color or filtering out) at each stage.

title: 3D Scene Editor
summary: To introduce the WebGL rendering context, 3D primitives, camera controls, and lighting models.
spec_text: A 3D viewport utilizing `orbitControl()`. The student can place 3D primitives (box, sphere, torus) and toggle different light sources (ambient, directional, point, spot). Different materials (basic, normal, ambient, specular) can be applied to see how they react to the lighting.

title: Synthesizer Board
summary: To teach sound generation, oscillators, ADSR envelopes, and basic audio routing.
spec_text: A virtual synthesizer interface utilizing the p5.sound library. The student routes a base oscillator through an ADSR envelope to generate notes. A visual waveform displays the shape of the sound (Sine, Square, Sawtooth, Triangle) as parameters are modified.

title: Audio Visualizer Lab
summary: To analyze sound frequencies and amplitudes using the Fast Fourier Transform (FFT).
spec_text: A real-time audio spectrum analyzer. It takes an audio input (microphone or file) and maps the FFT frequency bins to visual equalizer bars. The student can adjust smoothing and isolate specific frequency ranges (bass, mid, treble) to trigger visual thresholds.

title: Pixel Processing Pipeline
summary: To teach image loading, tinting, pixel-level manipulation, and convolution filters.
spec_text: An interactive image filter pipeline. The student loads a static image or webcam feed and applies sequential filters (grayscale, blur, threshold, posterize). A convolution matrix editor allows students to input custom kernel weights for edge detection and sharpening.

title: Kinetic Typography Engine
summary: To extract font paths and apply generative physics or parameters to text rendering.
spec_text: A text-to-points simulator. The student types a word, and the simulation converts the font glyphs into an array of vector points using `textToPoints()`. Sliders control the sampling density, and physical forces (wobble, explosion) can be applied to scatter the typography.

title: Dev Environment Simulator
summary: To simulate debugging, console logs, network errors (CORS), and developer tools.
spec_text: A mock 'IDE' layout featuring a code editor panel and a console output panel. The simulation injects intentional errors (like attempting to load a local image without a server). The student must use the mock console and network tabs to identify and 'fix' the configuration.

title: Pedagogical Pattern Matcher
summary: To train educators on identifying student misconceptions and selecting scaffolding strategies.
spec_text: A teacher-facing quiz-style simulation. A fictional student's buggy code or misunderstanding is presented. The user must classify the misconception (e.g., scoping error, translation order) and select the most appropriate pedagogical scaffolding (Parsons problem, live coding) to help the student.
